info.title: SalvageAlert Developer API
info.description:
REST API for real-time IAA and Copart salvage auction inventory across the US, Canada, UK and Germany. Unified Lot schema across all eight sources, plus an archived-inventory browse endpoint. Free tier: 50 credits on signup.

**Field conventions.** Timestamp units and boolean representation are NOT uniform across this API, and the exceptions are the ones that bite. Read `x-conventions` before you write a deserializer — it is four short rules and it is where the millisecond fields are named.

**Versioning.** Additive changes (new fields, new optional parameters, new endpoints) ship without notice and bump the minor version — treat unknown response fields as forgivable. Removals and meaning changes bump the major version and are announced first. Every version is listed with its date and its changes in `x-changelog`, newest first; diff that array rather than the whole spec. See `x-deprecation-policy` for what we promise before anything is removed.

x-conventions.rule: FOUR representations, and which one you get depends on the field, not the endpoint. (1) Epoch SECONDS — every `*_at` field, plus `archived_at`, `last_seen_utc`, `first_seen_utc`, `sold_at`, `created_at`, `enrolled_at` and the `since`/`until`/`updated_since` query parameters. This is the default; assume it unless named below. (2) Epoch MILLISECONDS — exactly two fields: `sale_date_utc` (snake_case objects) and `auctionDateUTC` (the camelCase Lot from /lots/search and /lots/{source}/{lot_key}). They are the same instant in the same unit under two names, and they are the only ms fields on the API. (3) ISO-8601 UTC strings — every timestamp inside the /matches.csv file, including its `sale_date_utc` column, because a spreadsheet will not open an epoch integer as a date. (4) `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar dates — `Usage.per_day[].day` (UTC days) and `FxRates.date` (passed through from the upstream reference source), which name a day rather than an instant and carry no time zone.
x-conventions.trap: Feeding `sale_date_utc` or `auctionDateUTC` to a seconds-based constructor lands you in the year 57,000; feeding a seconds field to a ms-based one lands you in 1970. Both fail silently and both have a plausible-looking date on the other side. Divide by 1000, do not guess by magnitude.

x-conventions.rule: Not uniform on InventoryLot, and both forms sit in the same object. `make_offer`, `wholesale_only`, `former_rental` and `offsite` are JSON booleans (`true`/`false`/`null`). `has_keys`, `drives` and `starts` are INTEGERS (`0`/`1`/`null`). All seven come from the same kind of source column and mean the same kind of thing; the split is history, not design.
x-conventions.trap: In a strictly typed client the three integers will not deserialize into a `bool?`. In a loosely typed one `if (lot.drives)` and `if (lot.offsite)` both work, and `lot.drives === true` silently never fires. Null means the source stated nothing — it is not `false`, for either form.
x-conventions.planned: Frozen for the life of v1: converting the three to booleans would break every client already reading them. v2 will make all seven booleans.

x-conventions.rule: Most endpoints return snake_case. /lots/search and /lots/{source}/{lot_key} return the raw normalized Lot object, which is camelCase (`stockNum`, `odometerReading`, `primaryDamage`, `imageUrl`, `auctionDateUTC`).

`current_bid` and `buy_now` are DISPLAY strings and may carry a currency symbol or a thousands separator. The numeric `*_value` fields — `buy_now_value`, `high_prebid_value`, `est_retail_value`, `acv` — are plain numbers. Sort, compare and chart on the `*_value` pair; never parse the strings. Each lot is in its own source currency (see the Source schema); only /stats/market normalizes to USD.

x-deprecation-policy.summary: Nothing that exists in v1 is removed from v1. Breaking changes land in a new major version at a new path, and v1 keeps serving what it serves today.
x-deprecation-policy.additive: New fields, new optional parameters and new endpoints ship without notice and bump the minor version. Your client MUST ignore response fields it does not recognise — that is the one thing we ask in return, and a strict deserializer that rejects unknown keys will break on a routine release.
x-deprecation-policy.breaking: Removing a field, narrowing a type, renaming anything, or changing what a value MEANS is breaking, and none of it happens inside v1. It happens in v2, on its own path, with both versions served in parallel.
x-deprecation-policy.notice: A field bound for removal in the next major is marked `deprecated: true` in this spec with a replacement named in its description, and stays that way for at least 90 days before the new major ships. Once v2 exists, v1 is supported for a minimum of 12 further months. Deprecations and sunset dates are announced in x-changelog and emailed to every account with a live key.
x-deprecation-policy.exceptions: Two things can change without that notice, because neither is a contract: the CONTENT of the auction data (a source restating a lot's damage or sale date), and anything we must change to close a security hole or honour a source's or a regulator's demand. Credit prices per endpoint and plan rate limits are commercial terms rather than API shape — those follow the billing terms, not this policy.

changes: New: GET, POST /api-keys and DELETE /api-keys/{id}. A key can be listed, minted and revoked one at a time over the API; /api-keys/rotate, which revokes every key, was the only key operation an integration had.
/me states the contract: `plan`, `monthly_credits`, `max_watches` and `max_webhooks`. A 409 was the only way to learn a limit.

/inventory/sources carries freshness per source: `newest_lot_at` and `newest_change_at` (Unix seconds) and a `stale` flag when nothing has changed for 48 hours, so a mirror can tell "no deltas" from "the crawler is down".

New: GET /inventory/{source}/{lot_key} — one catalogue lot by identity, off the index, every source, 1 credit on a hit and nothing on a miss. The only per-lot read was the live /lots/{source}/{lot_key}, refused for iaai_uk and govdeals_us.

New: GET and PATCH /matches/{id}. A match can be favorited, dismissed, annotated and priced over the API — max_bid_value, price_alert_value, notes, won and resale — which the web UI and the phones could do and an integration could not.

/matches rows now carry the annotations and the fields the CSV had and the JSON dropped: max_bid_value, price_alert_value, notes, resale_price, pinned_at, lane, run_number, sale_event_status, uk_category, condition_text, odometer_value/unit, has_carfax, and listing_url. The row is typed as the Match schema; it was an untyped object.
InventoryLot documents `damage_estimate_value` and `uk_category`, which /inventory has returned since 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-21 without a schema entry — a strict generated client dropped both.

Webhooks: three new `lot.updated` kinds — `bid_changed` (a favorite's bid jumped inside the 48h approach window), `max_bid_crossed` (the live bid passed the ceiling set on a favorite) and `price_drop` (a Buy Now price fell to the target set on a favorite). Each was already a Telegram, push and email alert and reached no webhook; a subscriber to `lot.updated` receives them now.

New: /vin-watches — list, create, read, update, delete and run the per-VIN watches that send `vin_watch_match` deliveries. They were the one resource an API key could not touch; the two notes below that said so are superseded.
New: GET /matches, the JSON pull path beside the CSV export, keyset-paged on `next_cursor`.
New: GET /auctions, the IAA and Copart sale calendar the site and the apps already show, with each Copart sale's yard and our catalogue count there.
New: POST /webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/redeliver replays a failed or dead delivery.

Webhooks: a reschedule is its own `kind`. A sale that had not run moving to another time (an hour or more) is delivered as `rescheduled`, with its own WebhookEventRescheduled schema; `relisted` stays for a sale that ran and a lot that came back.
/inventory takes the catalog's remaining filters: buy_now, clean_title, title, runs_drives, has_keys, ending_within_hours, location, yard, state, and sale_terms.
/vin/{vin}/history and /vin/batch: each lot carries `prior_sales`, the completed earlier auction cycles of that same lot number.

Webhooks: a relist is its own `kind`. A lot re-running under the same source and lot number was being delivered as `auction_result`, a shape that declares `result`, `before` and `after` required and carries none of them on a relist — so a receiver switching on `kind`, which is what the spec tells it to do, read `data.result` as undefined. It is `relisted` now, with its own WebhookEventRelisted schema.

Webhooks: the SSRF refusal for an RFC1918 / loopback / 169.254 ADDRESS is `private_address`, which is what the code has always emitted. `private_host` fires only for a hostname (localhost, .local, .internal). The spec named `private_host` for both, so a client branching on it never fired for the case it was written for.

/lots/{source}/{lot_key}/images and images.zip: copart_de is out of the `source` path enum. Both handlers refuse it and their own 400 descriptions said so — the enum offered an argument that always 400s.
`Lot.keys` and `Lot.drives` are `nullable: true`, matching `Lot.starts` and the runtime: all three are `boolean | null`, and IAA UK and GovDeals never report any of them.

Removed the "5 credits on a govdeals_us miss" clause from the three lot endpoints. It is unreachable: the single-lot route refuses govdeals before it queries, and neither image route serves it. The miss fee on those endpoints is 1 credit.

A 429 now carries X-Credits-Charged and X-Credits-Balance, which this spec has always documented on it. A client tracking its balance was losing the reading at exactly the moment it was being throttled.

Watch.active: corrected. Nothing on the server ever clears it — the VIN watches that stand themselves down once they find their vehicle are a separate resource (superseded: since 1.6.0 they are /vin-watches), so a `vin_watch_match` delivery does not come from a /watches filter set.
/lots/{source}/{lot_key}/images: `limit` max and default are 50, not 100. The IAA enumeration walks a single prefix and stops at 50, so a higher value could never be honoured.

images.zip: the archive holds up to 136 entries on IAA (100 photos plus up to 36 exterior-360 frames), and the `<stock>_<year>_<make>_<model>.zip` filename is IAA-only — the Copart path reads the gallery endpoint directly and never loads the lot, so it is `lot_<lot_key>.zip`.
`WebhookEventVinWatchMatch.match_id` is not a column in /v1/matches.csv. Join a delivery to an export on (source, lot_key).
`VinHistoryLot.vin` is nullable — IAA publishes a masked VIN on most lots and those rows carry null.

The `Lot` schema declares the ~18 fields it was serializing and not documenting: ukCategory, isTimedAuction, the auction* identifiers, auctionBranch*, buyNowClosingDateUTC, stockBranchId, yardPhynumb, lane, runNumber, reserveStatus, hasCarfax, airbags, lossType and physicalCountry. Additive for anyone ignoring unknown keys; a generated model was missing a third of the lot.
Every operation now declares the 429 it can return — only two of thirty-two did — plus the 404 on the five webhook-by-id operations, the 400 on /models, and the three 400s on POST /watches.
/vehicles/vin/{vin}: the documented year range 1981-2100 is enforced. Out of range was reaching vPIC and coming back as a 502; it is a 400 `invalid_year`.

/inventory: `include_sold=true` now returns the ended lots our own staleness sweep had hidden — 307,896 across the seven sources, 223,298 of them Copart US. The gate could not tell our crawler's "we stopped seeing this" from a user hiding a lot inside their own account, and refused both; it now refuses only the second. Every one of those lots was already browsable on salvagealert.com/lots.

/inventory: documented that a lot returned under `include_sold` may be ended with a NULL `sold_at` — a source can stop listing a lot without a sale we can record — so read a past `sale_date_utc` as ended too.
Added `x-conventions`: the timestamp units and the boolean representation, stated once at the top of the spec instead of only per-field.
Documented `Lot.auctionDateUTC` as epoch MILLISECONDS. It had no unit at all, and every other integer timestamp on the camelCase Lot is seconds — so it read as seconds and is not.
Documented that every timestamp inside the /matches.csv file is an ISO-8601 UTC string, including its `sale_date_utc` column.

Documented the boolean/integer split on InventoryLot: `has_keys`, `drives` and `starts` are 0/1 integers while `make_offer`, `wholesale_only`, `former_rental` and `offsite` are booleans. Frozen for v1; all seven become booleans in v2.
Added `x-deprecation-policy`: nothing is removed from v1, 90 days marked `deprecated` before a new major, 12 months of parallel support after it.
Watches: added PATCH /watches/{id} `{active?, label?}`. Pausing a watch no longer requires DELETE + POST, so the watch id survives it.

X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset now describe a continuously refilling allowance: the limiter is a token bucket that survives a deploy, not a window that empties on restart. Retry-After is unchanged and is still the number to obey on a 429.
/inventory: added `updated_since` and `cursor` for stable keyset pagination and incremental sync; `page` is now capped at 500 and is documented as unsafe for bulk mirroring.
/inventory: lots now carry `gallery_urls` (the full mirrored photo set, free) alongside `image_url`.
Webhooks: every `data` payload now carries a `kind` discriminator, and all five payload shapes are documented as WebhookEvent* schemas.
Webhooks: documented the auto-disable threshold, the retry/backoff schedule, and `format` — including that discord/slack deliveries are NOT HMAC-signed.
Webhooks: the owner is now emailed when a subscription is auto-disabled.
/webhooks/{id}/deliveries: `latency_ms` renamed to `queue_delay_ms` — it never measured the receiver, only queue wait.
/vin/batch: VINs that return no lots are no longer billed, matching /vin/{vin}/history. Added `looked_up`.
/yards: response is now a real oneOf per source instead of an untyped object.
/api-keys/rotate: documented as account-wide and destructive; the owner is now emailed on rotation.
Documented every error code, the X-Salvagealert-Warning header, /me's 404, and the read-only nature of Watch.active.

/inventory: lots gained acv, title_state, origin_country, sale_event_status, sale_light, autograde, make_offer, wholesale_only, former_rental, offsite/offsite_location, lane, run_number, airbags_status, loss_type, has_keys, drives, starts, trim, and later high_prebid_value, buy_now_value and sold_at.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Push notifications on new matches.

**Envelope.** Every delivery is a POST whose body is `{ event, created_at, data }` — `event` is one of `lot.matched` / `lot.updated` / `lot.sold`, `created_at` is unix SECONDS, and `data` is one of the six WebhookEvent* shapes. Each `data` carries a `kind` discriminator; switch on it, not on the presence of a field. See the WebhookDelivery schema.

**Retries.** A delivery is attempted up to 7 times with a fixed backoff — 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 8 hours, then 24 hours — roughly 35 hours end to end, after which it is marked `dead` and dropped. A 4xx other than 408 or 429 is treated as a permanent refusal and is not retried at all; 2xx is success; anything else (5xx, timeout, connection error) is retried. We do NOT follow redirects — a 3xx is a failure. Timeout is 15 seconds. Deliveries are not ordered and may arrive more than once, so make your receiver idempotent.

**Auto-disable.** After 20 CONSECUTIVE failed deliveries the subscription itself is switched off (`active` becomes false) and everything still queued for it is dropped. The counter resets to 0 on any success, so it takes a sustained outage, not a bad afternoon — but a receiver down for a long maintenance window WILL be disabled, and events that occur while it is off are not backfilled when you turn it back on. The account owner is emailed when this happens. Re-enable with PATCH /webhooks/{id} `{"active": true}`.

**Signing depends on `format`.** Only `generic` deliveries carry the `X-Salvagealert-Signature` HMAC. See the Webhook schema — this is a security property and the format is auto-detected from your URL.

post.description: Search lots from one source. Cache hits cost 0 credits. Each source pushes down the filters its site can apply (keyword everywhere; year, damage, title and price on IAA Canada; make and year on the Copart feed; a single make on IAA US and GovDeals), and every page is then run through the same local gate the app uses, so a filter the source cannot apply still holds — the lots it removes are counted in `filtered_out`. A cache hit is never refused for balance: the pre-authorisation checks the cache first, so an account at 0 credits can still replay a cached page. A page can therefore be short or empty while `total_estimate` is large: `total_estimate` is the source's own count for the part of the request it applied, not the count after the gate. Keep paging by `page`, not by comparing lots seen to `total_estimate`.

get.summary: Fetch a single lot by stock #
get.description: Always bypasses cache so bids and sale state are live. 1 credit on a hit. On copart_us and copart_ca the source of truth is the Copart Sales Data feed we import three times a day (08:00, 14:00, 19:00 New York time), not a live page fetch, so a lot is at most a few hours old there; IAA and GovDeals lookups hit the auction live. A lot the source no longer lists — sold and removed, or withdrawn — is a 404 here even while /inventory still carries it; see `Lot.isAuctionClosed` for how to read sale status on a hit. A miss is not free: the lookup still fires a live source query, so a 404 that ran that query is charged a reduced miss fee of 1 credit. Request-shape 400s cost nothing, and so does an unsupported source, which is refused before any query runs. The exact amount is on X-Credits-Charged.

get.description:
Page through the public archived-inventory index — the same de-duplicated, continuously-crawled catalogue behind salvagealert.com/lots. Reads pre-archived stock from our index (no live source fetch). Costs 1 credit per call.

**Two pagination modes. Only one of them is safe for bulk.**

`page` is an OFFSET into a table the poller and three crawlers write to continuously. It is correct for jumping to a page a person will read, and wrong for mirroring: at page_size=100 a full walk of the catalogue is thousands of requests, rows shift underneath it throughout, and the walk silently skips and duplicates lots. It is capped at page 500.

`cursor` is the keyset mode and is what you want for a mirror. Results are ordered by (archived_at, source, lot_key) ascending; pass the `next_cursor` from the previous response to resume, and stop when it comes back null. A lot the crawler re-touches mid-walk moves to the END of that ordering — which the walk has not reached — so it is re-emitted rather than skipped. Send `cursor` or `updated_since` (or both) to select this mode; `page` and `sort` are then ignored, because the ordering IS the cursor.

`updated_since` (unix SECONDS, compared against `archived_at`) is the incremental half: having mirrored once, ask only for what has changed rather than re-walking the whole catalogue at a credit a page. Combine it with `cursor` to page through a large delta. `archived_at` moves whenever a lot CHANGES — bid, sale date, photo, identity, a sale — and not on a re-crawl that found it unchanged, so a delta is exactly the lots whose details changed plus those new to you; upsert on (source, lot_key). With `include_sold=true` the delta also carries the lots that sold since, each with its `sold_at`.

Lots deleted from our catalogue are NOT reported by this endpoint — a mirror should treat a lot it has not seen for a while as stale rather than expecting a tombstone.

**Ended lots are opt-in.** By default the endpoint returns live stock only, so every row has `sold_at` null. Send `include_sold=true` to receive the ended archive too: lots that sold, and lots the source stopped listing without a sale we could record. The second kind can carry a null `sold_at`, so treat a `sale_date_utc` in the past as ended rather than reading `sold_at` alone. It works in both pagination modes and combines with `updated_since`, since a sale moves `archived_at`. What it never returns is a lot a SalvageAlert account holder hid from their own view — a lot OUR crawler simply stopped seeing is catalogue history, and is returned.

As of 2026-09-02 each lot also carries acv, title_state, origin_country, sale_event_status, sale_light, autograde, make_offer, wholesale_only, former_rental, offsite/offsite_location, lane, run_number, airbags_status, loss_type, has_keys, drives, starts and trim — additive, so existing integrations are unaffected. As of 2026-09-04 it also carries high_prebid_value, buy_now_value and sold_at, so prices can be sorted and charted without parsing the formatted current_bid/buy_now strings, and an ended lot can be told from a live one.

post.description:
**Privileged and irreversible.** Revokes EVERY active key on the account — not just the one that made this call — and mints a single fresh key. The raw secret is returned ONCE and cannot be retrieved again; only its hash and display prefix are stored.

It costs 0 credits and requires no re-authentication beyond the bearer key itself, which means a leaked key can rotate the account and lock out its legitimate owner. The account owner is emailed on every rotation — if you receive that mail and did not rotate, rotate again to cut the holder off and check your API usage log.

post.description:
The HMAC `secret` is returned exactly once on creation and cannot be retrieved afterwards.

The URL must be absolute https — plain http is refused with `non_https`. It is validated on creation AND re-validated at every delivery, so a host that later resolves into a private range stops being delivered to: private / RFC1918 / loopback / cloud-metadata addresses are refused (`private_address`), as are unresolvable hosts (`dns_unresolvable`), URLs carrying `user:pass@` (`credentials_in_url`) and anything unparseable (`invalid_url`). A URL that starts failing this check counts toward the 20-failure auto-disable like any other failure.

`format` defaults to whatever your URL looks like — see the Webhook schema, and note that a Discord or Slack URL disables HMAC signing.

post.description:
Saved filter set that triggers `lot.matched` events (kind `watch_match`). filters JSON is capped at 4 KB — over it, 400 `watch_filters_too_large`.

To pause a watch, PATCH it with `{"active": false}` and PATCH it back when you want it firing again — the id survives, so anything you correlate on it keeps working. `active` is YOURS ALONE: nothing on the server ever clears it. A `vin_watch_match` delivery comes from the per-VIN watches, a different feature that stands itself down once it finds its vehicle; those live under /vin-watches.

`source` and `filters` are fixed at creation. They define what the watch IS, so changing them would repoint an id you are already correlating on — POST a new watch instead.

WHAT A WATCH SEES: lots as they are INGESTED BY A SAVED SEARCH — this account's or any other's. It is not the whole catalogue. The bulk imports that also fill it (the daily Copart sales feed, the archive crawl, the Buy Now crawl) do not fan out to watches, so a lot that only ever arrives that way appears in `/v1/inventory` without ever having triggered a watch. Poll `/v1/inventory` with `updated_since` when you need every lot; use a watch when you want to be told about the ones people are actively tracking.

get.description:
Aggregate price snapshot for a make (and optional model) across the whole archive. Costs 1 credit.

**What the price actually is.** Each distinct lot — one row per (source, lot number) — contributes its Buy Now price if it has one, otherwise its highest pre-bid, converted to USD at the current reference rate. That is the best price we hold for the lot, NOT a confirmed sale price: most salvage lots sell on approval and the hammer price is never published, so nothing here is a "winning bid". Treat it as the asking/bidding level, not the settlement.

**Which lots each number counts.** `lot_count` is every distinct lot matching the make/model, priced or not. `avg_bid`, `median_bid`, `min_bid` and `max_bid` are computed over the SUBSET that carries a price above zero, which is smaller and is not currently returned — so `avg_bid × lot_count` is not a market total. `avg_retail_value` is likewise averaged only over lots carrying a pre-loss retail estimate. `median_bid` is the lower of the two middle values on an even count. No outlier trimming is applied: a mistyped 9,999,999 bid in a feed moves `max_bid` and `avg_bid` and leaves `median_bid` alone, which is why the median is the number to build on.

avg_bid.description: Mean USD price over the priced subset only. Null when no lot carries a price.

median_bid.description: Median USD price over the priced subset (lower middle value on an even count). Untrimmed, but unlike the mean it is unmoved by a single bad feed value.

min_bid.description: Lowest USD price above zero in the priced subset.

max_bid.description: Highest USD price in the priced subset. Untrimmed — a single mistyped feed value lands here.

avg_retail_value.description: Mean pre-loss retail estimate in USD, over the lots that carry one. A different, usually smaller, subset again.

ErrorCode.description:
Every `error.code` the API emits.

**Authentication (401).** `missing_credentials` — no or malformed Authorization header. `invalid_credentials` — the key is unknown or revoked. `account_inactive` — the key is valid but the account behind it is no longer active; rotating will not help, contact support. `key_revoked_missing_project_url` — the key was swept on 2026-10-01 because it named no project URL. Set one at /app/api and rotate; see the X-Salvagealert-Warning header, which warns about this on every response BEFORE the deadline. A key whose owning user record is gone answers `account_inactive`.

**Account (403).** `api_disabled` — the account is not enrolled for API access or an operator switched it off; the key is valid. Contact support.

**Quota (402 / 429).** `insufficient_credits` — the call was pre-authorised against your balance and refused; X-Credits-Balance carries what you actually have. `rate_limit` — over the per-minute allowance for your plan; Retry-After names the second a slot frees.

**Request shape (400, never billed).** `invalid_source` / `unsupported_source` — unknown source, or one this particular endpoint does not serve (image endpoints are IAA + Copart only). `invalid_location` (/lots/search) — a `locations` token the source cannot resolve, listed under `unknown_locations`; it is refused rather than silently widened. `invalid_title_type` (/lots/search) — a `title_types` value outside clean / salvage / rebuilt / parts. `invalid_sort`, `invalid_cursor`, `invalid_updated_since` (/inventory). `invalid_json`, `missing_vins`, `no_valid_vins`, `too_many_vins` (/vin/batch, max 50). `invalid_make_id` (/models). `invalid_year` (/vehicles/vin/{vin}) — outside 1981-2100, the range the 17-character VIN standard covers. `watch_filters_too_large` (/watches, 4 KB cap). `invalid_body` — the body was not JSON, or (PATCH /watches/{id}) named none of the patchable fields. `invalid_active` / `invalid_label` (PATCH /watches/{id}) — the field was sent with the wrong type. Webhook URL rejections: `invalid_url`, `credentials_in_url` (no `user:pass@`), `private_address` (an RFC1918, loopback or 169.254 cloud-metadata ADDRESS, which is the code this check actually emits), `private_host` (a HOSTNAME — localhost, .local or .internal), `dns_unresolvable`, `non_https`. `invalid_events` (webhooks) — an event name outside the documented set. `invalid_filters` (POST /watches) — `filters` is not a JSON object. `invalid_bid` (/fees/estimate) — `bid` is not a positive number. `invalid_tax_region` (/fees/estimate) — `tax_region` is not one the source's country can charge: QC/ON for the Canadian sources, a US state for the US ones, and none at all for iaai_uk / copart_uk / copart_de, which price a flat VAT. It is refused rather than applied by name — the fee tables are keyed on the region name alone, so `CA` would otherwise put California sales tax on a Canadian lot. `unsupported_source` — the source exists but this endpoint cannot serve it (single-lot lookup on iaai_uk / govdeals_us, galleries on copart_de, iaai_uk, govdeals_us).

**Not found (404).** `not_found` — the webhook or watch id is not yours or does not exist. `lot_not_found` — no lot with that stock number; a live source query still ran, so a reduced miss fee is charged. `no_photos` / `no_anchor_image` — the lot exists but has no gallery; also charged the miss fee. `no_data` — no lots matched a market-stats query.

**Upstream (502).** `upstream_unavailable` — a third-party service (NHTSA vPIC decode, safety, fuel economy, FX) did not answer, rate-limited us, or failed. Transient; retry with backoff. An upstream 429 or 5xx is always reported here and never as a request error: `invalid_vin` / `invalid_params` mean YOUR parameters, so they are worth debugging, and they used to be returned for an upstream rate limit as well.

**Server (500).** `internal_error` — our fault; never billed. Quote `request_id` when reporting it. `no_photos_fetched` — every photo URL failed to download; free, retry.

monthly_credits.description: Credits the plan grants on each subscription period (free 0 / starter 500 / unlimited 5000). Top-up packs come on top.

max_watches.description: How many active /watches the plan allows; POST /watches answers 409 too_many_lot_watches past it.

max_webhooks.description: How many webhook destinations the plan allows.

credit_balance.description: May be fractional — some endpoints cost 0.2 credits.

rate_limit_per_minute.description: The allowance actually enforced on your next call — the same number the X-RateLimit-Limit header carries. Normally your plan's (free 60 / starter 120 / unlimited 300), or a higher per-account limit if support has granted you one.

keyword.description: Free-text query. Every word must appear in the lot's make, model or brand (AND), on every source.

locations.description: ISO state/province codes (US-FL, CA-QC, CA-SK, …), OR-ed together; empty means everywhere. iaai_ca also takes its six regions (QC, ON, AB, BC, ATL, PRAIRIES) and numeric branch ids from /v1/yards, mixed freely — CA-SK covers every Saskatchewan yard, which is where the SGI sales run. copart_uk / copart_de take their region codes from /v1/yards (UK-ENG, DE-BY). iaai_uk is one national catalogue and accepts only UK-ALL. A token the source cannot resolve is refused with 400 `invalid_location` rather than ignored. On Copart and GovDeals the location is applied to each page after the fetch, so `total_estimate` there is the count before it.

title_types.description: Keep only these title buckets (OR-ed). A lot whose source reports no title status at all (GovDeals, some Copart lots) is kept, not dropped. Any other value is refused with 400 `invalid_title_type`.

page_size.description: The page size the source actually uses. Usually what you asked for; iaai_uk is fixed at 20.

total_estimate.description: The source's own count for the filters it applied itself, before the local gate. GovDeals reports the size of the page. An upper bound on what paging will yield, never the exact number.

filtered_out.description: Lots the source returned on this page that the local gate removed because they did not match a filter the source could not apply. Explains a short page.

cached.description: Whether this response was served from the shared search cache (0 credits).

Lot.description: Normalized vehicle lot. Fields are population-best-effort — null/missing means the source did not provide the value.

auctionDate.description: The sale date as the auction displays it. Free text, source-formatted; parse `auctionDateUTC` instead.

auctionDateUTC.description: Epoch MILLISECONDS of the auction/close time, or null when the source has not assigned one. Milliseconds, like `sale_date_utc` — NOT seconds, unlike every `*_at` field on this API. Divide by 1000 before handing it to a seconds-based date constructor.

isAuctionClosed.description: The sale for this lot is over: it ran and the source still lists it (sold on approval, awaiting relist). Always false when `auctionDateUTC` is in the future or null. Sale status is therefore: `auctionDateUTC` null → not yet assigned to a sale; in the future → upcoming; in the past or `isAuctionClosed` → ended. A withdrawn or sold-and-removed lot no longer exists at the source, so GET /lots/{source}/{lot_key} answers 404 `lot_not_found` for it even while /inventory (the daily catalogue) still lists it.

ukCategory.description: UK ABI salvage category (SYNETIQ / Copart UK only). Absent elsewhere — non-UK lots are classified by `brandCodeType`.

auctionDateTimeDisplay.description: The sale time as the auction prints it. Free text; parse `auctionDateUTC`.

auction.description: Sale event name, e.g. "MPI Regional Sale".

auctionBranchId.description: Set when the sale happens somewhere other than the storage yard.

buyNowClosingDateUTC.description: Epoch MILLISECONDS the Buy Now price expires — same unit as `auctionDateUTC`.

yardPhynumb.description: Copart numeric yard id. The camelCase twin of InventoryLot.yard_id.

lane.description: Auction-day lane. Short source-formatted string ("1", "B"). Absent for Copart and for lots not yet assigned a slot. The camelCase twin of InventoryLot.lane.

runNumber.description: Auction-day run number, same shape and same caveats as `lane`. The camelCase twin of InventoryLot.run_number.

hasCarfax.description: Copart only: a Carfax report is available for this lot.

physicalCountry.description: Where the vehicle physically is, derived from the yard. Copart Canada surfaces US-located lots open to Canadian bidders, so this can differ from the source country.

InventoryResponse.description: One page of inventory. Which optional keys are present depends on `mode`: offset mode returns `page`, `max_page` and `total`; keyset mode returns `next_cursor`, `has_more` and `updated_since`, with `total` null.

source.description: Echoes the `source` filter, or null when unfiltered.

mode.description: Which pagination mode answered this request. `cursor` whenever `cursor` or `updated_since` was sent.

page.description: Offset mode only. The page actually served — clamped to `max_page`, so it can be lower than the `page` you asked for.

max_page.description: Offset mode only. The deepest page this endpoint will serve (500). Past it, switch to `cursor`.

total.description: Total matching lots across all pages. NULL in keyset mode: counting costs a second full walk of the catalogue per page, and a total that moves while you walk is not a number a mirror can act on. Use `has_more` / `next_cursor` to drive the loop instead.

sort.description: The sort applied. Always `updated_asc` in keyset mode — the ordering IS the cursor, so `sort` is ignored there.

updated_since.description: Keyset mode. Echoes the `updated_since` you sent, or null.

next_cursor.description: Keyset mode. Pass verbatim as `cursor` to get the next page. NULL means you have reached the end of the walk — stop.

has_more.description: Keyset mode. False on the last page.

InventoryLot.description: A single archived lot from the public inventory index. snake_case projection; null means the source did not provide the value.

sale_date_utc.description: Unix ms of the auction/close time when known.

current_bid.description: Formatted for display. Sort or chart on high_prebid_value instead.

buy_now.description: Formatted for display. Sort or chart on buy_now_value instead.

high_prebid_value.description: The current/high bid as a plain number, in the lot's own currency.

buy_now_value.description: The Buy Now price as a plain number, in the lot's own currency.

damage_estimate_value.description: The auction's repair estimate as a plain number, in the lot's own currency. Copart publishes it on most lots; IAA rarely.

uk_category.description: UK ABI salvage category letter (A, B, S, N; C and D on older lots). Null outside the UK sources.

acv.description: Actual Cash Value — the insurer's valuation of the vehicle BEFORE the loss. The anchor for judging whether a bid is good. IAA publishes this on most lots; Copart does not.

title_state.description: Two-letter state or province that issued the title. Branding rules differ by jurisdiction, so the same title wording is not the same fact everywhere.

origin_country.description: Where the vehicle was built, as reported by the auction.

sale_event_status.description: How the sale runs. "Pure Sale" — the high bid wins outright. "On Approval" — the seller may still refuse it. "On Minimum Bid" — a floor applies. Copart only.

sale_light.description: Copart's run-condition light. RED flags a known problem.

autograde.description: Copart's numeric condition grade, where published.

make_offer.description: The lot accepts offers as well as bids, on the auction's own site.

wholesale_only.description: Restricted to licensed dealers. A retail buyer cannot bid.

offsite_location.description: Where the vehicle actually is, when that is NOT vehicle_location. Copart publishes the address.

offsite.description: The vehicle is stored away from the branch in vehicle_location. IAA Canada flags this without publishing an address, so this can be true while offsite_location is null.

lane.description: Auction lane. IAA only — Copart does not publish it.

run_number.description: Run order within the lane. IAA only.

loss_type.description: Cause of loss: Collision, Water, Fire, Theft, Other.

has_keys.description: Keys present. INTEGER 0/1, not a boolean — see `x-conventions`. Null means the source stated nothing.

drives.description: Drive-verified. INTEGER 0/1, not a boolean — see `x-conventions`. Null means the source stated nothing.

starts.description: Start-verified. INTEGER 0/1, not a boolean — see `x-conventions`. Null means the source stated nothing. Note iaai_us has no separate starts signal (see v140), so its zeros were cleared to null rather than asserting a verified non-starter.

image_url.description: The anchor photo, mirrored onto our own image host. Also the first entry in `gallery_urls`.

gallery_urls.description: Every photo we hold for this lot, mirrored onto our own image host — no extra credits and no live source fetch. Use this instead of /lots/{source}/{lot_key}/images (4 credits) unless you specifically need a resolution we do not mirror. Single-element while the mirror has only reached the anchor shot, and empty when the lot has no usable photo.

listing_url.description: Canonical public SalvageAlert listing page for this lot.

archived_at.description: Unix seconds this lot last CHANGED — a new bid, sale date, photo, identity, or a sale (sold_at set) — or was first seen, for a lot that has not changed since. It does not move on a re-crawl that found the lot unchanged, so an updated_since delta is lots that changed, not lots we merely looked at.

sold_at.description: Unix seconds the lot stopped being listed at the source. That is a sale on most lots, but it also covers a withdrawal, so read it as "no longer offered" rather than as a confirmed sale. It carries no price: a final sale price is only available where Copart's daily sales-data file covers the lot, which is the United States and Canada. Null means still listed. Sold lots are only returned when `include_sold=true` is sent, so on a default walk this is always null.

active.description: False means nothing is being delivered. It is set false automatically after 20 consecutive failures; set it back with PATCH /webhooks/{id}.

failure_count.description: CONSECUTIVE failed deliveries. Reset to 0 by any success. At 20 the subscription is auto-disabled (`active` becomes false), queued deliveries for it are dropped, and the account owner is emailed.

format.description: Receiver dialect, and a SECURITY-relevant field. `generic` posts the canonical `{ event, created_at, data }` envelope AND is the only format that carries the `X-Salvagealert-Signature` HMAC header — Discord and Slack deliveries are re-rendered into their own message shapes and sent with NO signature at all, on the reasoning that those receivers authenticate by possession of a secret URL. The consequence is that a Discord or Slack endpoint cannot verify a delivery actually came from us, and anyone who learns the URL can post to it. The value is AUTO-DETECTED from your URL when you do not send one (discord.com or discordapp.com /api/webhooks/*, hooks.slack.com /services/*), so a subscriber who happens to post to one of those hosts silently loses signing. Set `generic` explicitly to keep the HMAC.

response_body_preview.description: Only populated for 2xx responses; non-2xx and errors get an opaque tag.

queue_delay_ms.description: How long the delivery waited in the queue before we attempted it — `last_attempted_at` minus `created_at`, in ms. This is NOT your receiver's response time; we do not currently measure that. A delivery that backed off for a day reads 86400000 here, which is the backoff working, not a slow endpoint. Was named `latency_ms` before 1.2.0, which described neither what it measured nor what it was used for.

filters.description: Same shape as SearchFilters used by the dashboard.

active.description: Whether the watch is firing. You own it: set it with PATCH /watches/{id}, and nothing on the server ever changes it. (The VIN watches that stand themselves down once they find their vehicle are a separate feature, under /vin-watches.)

last_match_at.description: Unix SECONDS of the most recent match, or null if it has never fired.

WatchPatch.description: At least one field. Omitted fields are left unchanged; an empty body is a 400.

active.description: False pauses the watch, true resumes it. The id does not change.

label.description: Longer values are truncated to 80 characters. Null clears it.

filters.description: SearchFilters shape; serialised filters_json capped at 4 KB.

active.description: False after a pause, and after the watch found its vehicle and stood itself down. Set it true to re-arm.

region.description: Where the active sweep searches; null for a passive-only watch.

last_run_at.description: Unix SECONDS of the last active sweep.

can_run_at.description: Unix SECONDS from which /run is allowed again; null when it can run now or has no region.

items.description: A lot the watch found: source, lot_key, year/make/model, sale_date_utc, the price fields, and public_lot_path.

events.description: What happened to the car after the watch fired, newest first.

region.description: Turns on the active keyword sweep; requires `sources` inside the region.

model_recognized.description: true when NHTSA holds this model for that make/year (a recall or an NCAP rating is itself proof). null when its model catalogue could not be read — the figures below still stand, but "no recalls" is unconfirmed. An unrecognised model is a 404, so this is never false.

rated_variants.description: Every NCAP-rated variant for this year/make/model. `ratings` describes the first of them.

variant.description: The variant these stars belong to — same value as `description`, named so it cannot be mistaken for a rating of the whole model line.

variants_available.description: How many variants NHTSA rates for this year/make/model; see `rated_variants`.

trims_available.description: How many EPA records exist for this year/make/model.

trims.description: Every trim available, in EPA menu order. Pass one back as ?trim=.

trim.description: The trim the figures below describe — the first listed unless ?trim= named another.

co2_g_per_mile.description: Tailpipe CO2. 0 is a real value (battery-electric); unknown is null.

CopartYardList.description: copart_ca / copart_us — the physical yard catalogue.

code.description: Yard code as Copart spells it in its own URL slugs.

IaaCaBranchList.description: iaai_ca — the .NET provincial branch catalogue. Note the element shape differs from Copart: the identifier is a NUMERIC `id`, not a `code`, and the region field is `province`.

id.description: IAA branch id. Pass it (as a string) in /lots/search `locations`, alone or beside province codes.

EmptyYardList.description: iaai_uk / iaai_us / copart_uk / copart_de / govdeals_us — these sources have no enumerable yard catalogue. `yards` is an empty array BY DESIGN and `note` says what to pass to /lots/search instead (ISO state codes for iaai_us; nothing at all for the rest, which browse country-wide). An empty array here is the answer, not a failure.

WebhookDelivery.description: The body POSTed to your endpoint, for `format: generic`. Discord and Slack subscriptions receive their own message shapes instead — and no signature. `data` is one of the six WebhookEvent* shapes (five events and the test fire); switch on `data.kind`, which is present on all of them.

created_at.description: Unix SECONDS the event was enqueued — not when it was delivered.

source_url.description: Deep link to the lot on the auction site.

last_seen_utc.description: Epoch seconds we last observed the lot.

prior_sales.description: Completed earlier auction cycles of this same lot number (sold on approval and refused, then re-run), newest first, each with the last bid we recorded before the sale date moved. Empty when the lot has run once.

sale_date_utc.description: Epoch milliseconds of the earlier sale.

WebhookEventTest.description: The `data` of a `webhook.test` fire from POST /webhooks/{id}/test.

WebhookEventWatchMatch.description: event `lot.matched` — a /v1/watches filter set matched a newly crawled lot.

watch_id.description: The Watch that fired. Absent on the vin_watch_match variant.

lot.description: The full camelCase Lot — the same object /lots/search returns, NOT the snake_case InventoryLot.

WebhookEventVinWatchMatch.description: event `lot.matched` — a VIN watch found its vehicle. Carries `vin_watch_id`, NOT `watch_id`: these are different subscriptions and the ids are not interchangeable. The VIN watch stands itself down after firing, so expect exactly one of these per listing found.

match_id.description: Our internal match row id — stable for the life of the row. NOT a column in /v1/matches.csv, which carries `search_id` and the lot identifiers; join a delivery to an export on (`source`, `lot_key`) instead.

WebhookEventClosingSoon.description: event `lot.updated` — bid movement on a tracked lot whose auction is about to start. Fires repeatedly while the price moves, so treat it as a state update rather than a one-shot.

search_id.description: The saved search that owns this match.

closing_in_seconds.description: Seconds until the scheduled sale time. Clamped at 0; never negative.

WebhookEventAuctionResult.description: event `lot.updated` — the auction concluded. Sent after a grace window, not the moment the sale time passes, because the live lane runs on past it.

WebhookEventRelisted.description: event `lot.updated` — a lot you already know about is running again under the SAME source and lot number, with a new sale date. Copart and IAA re-run a lot that sold on approval and was refused, which is why the identifiers do not change. Carries no price snapshot: nothing about the money has happened yet.

won.description: Present and true when you had marked this lot WON: the sale was not honoured and the lot runs again.

sale_date_utc.description: Unix MILLISECONDS of the new sale time.

WebhookEventRescheduled.description: event `lot.updated` — a sale that had NOT run yet moved to another time, by an hour or more. Distinct from `relisted`, where the sale ran and the lot is back. Carries no price snapshot.

sale_date_utc.description: Unix MILLISECONDS of the new sale time.

WebhookEventBidChanged.description: event `lot.updated` — the bid on a FAVORITED lot jumped, inside the 48-hour approach window before its sale. Fires once per meaningful jump (the same threshold as the bid-up alert), so a lot climbing steadily produces several.

closing_in_seconds.description: Seconds until the scheduled sale time. Clamped at 0.

WebhookEventMaxBidCrossed.description: event `lot.updated` — the live bid on a favorited lot passed the ceiling its owner set on it. Once per ceiling: it re-arms only when the ceiling is raised.

WebhookEventPriceDrop.description: event `lot.updated` — a favorited lot's Buy Now price fell to or under the target its owner set. Once per target: it re-arms only when the target is changed.

buy_now_value.description: The Buy Now price that met it.

WebhookEventDelisted.description: event `lot.sold` — the lot stopped appearing in its source feed, so we closed it out. "Sold" is our inference from the delisting, not a settlement confirmed by the auction house.

final_bid.description: The last bid we observed, in `currency`. Not necessarily the hammer price.

sold_at.description: Unix SECONDS we closed the lot out.

prefix.description: The first characters of the key, safe to display. The secret itself is never returned after minting.

current.description: The key this request was authenticated with.

key.description: The full secret. Shown once; store it now.

Match.description: One lot a saved search matched, as the CSV export spells it plus your own annotations. Timestamps are Unix SECONDS except `sale_date_utc`, which is MILLISECONDS. `current_bid` and `buy_now` are display strings; sort and compare on the `*_value` numbers, in `currency`.

matched_at.description: When the search first saw the lot. Never moves.

vin.description: Masked on most anonymously-scraped rows; full where a crawl had it.

sale_event_status.description: "Pure Sale", "On Approval", "On Minimum Bid". Copart only.

detail_url.description: The auction house's page. Taken down about two days after a sale.

listing_url.description: Our own page for the lot, which outlives the auction house's.

price_alert_value.description: Your Buy Now target, in `currency`. Writable.

notes.description: Your private note, up to 2000 characters. Writable.

resale_price.description: What you sold it on for. Writable on a won lot.

won_repair_cost.description: Your repair cost on a won lot, in `currency`.

MatchPatch.description: Any subset. An omitted field is left alone; null clears a price or the note.

won.description: true marks the lot won (with `won_price` if given); false clears won, won_price and resale_price.

WebhookPriceSnapshot.description: Price state either side of the change. Both fields are plain numbers in the lot's own currency.

date.description: The reference date these rates were published for, `YYYY-MM-DD`, passed through from the upstream reference source. No time and no zone: it names a day. Empty string on the rare response where upstream omitted it.
